claims.text: On the document Fouche calls the SAC-DARPA Classified Document: 'This letter is UNCLASSIFIED. It was never marked as classified material (no classification markings, no control number, no Copy X of Y). There is nothing unusual about the letterhead. Use of the DoD seal is standard. The letter was signed by the NCO in Charge, Airman Aircraft Maintenance Assignments Section, Office of the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel... Where it says REPLY TO: DARPA, this might be a five-letter office code (such as DPAQR, the Command Records Branch at SAC HQ). This letter simply indicates that the Air Force Manpower and Personnel Center (AFMPC) has approved an After Action Review (or Report)'. The page image opened by this research corroborates the absence of any classification marking and the signature block he describes.

edges.label: Reads the 'SAC/DARPA Classified Document' as an unclassified personnel letter from a personnel office
edges.note: Two parts of Merlin's reading were checked independently against the page image and hold: there is no classification marking of any kind on the letter, and the signature block does place the originating office inside the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel, which is what his five-letter-office-code reading of 'REPLY TO: DARPA' predicts. His gloss of AAR as After Action Review was not verified against any Air Force instruction.

edges.label: Named aerospace historian; four falsifiable specifics against the claimant's evidence
edges.note: 'I have always been extremely skeptical of Fouche. Many of his claims were questionable or misleading.' The four specifics are on the peter-merlin node in full: the letter is unclassified; the 'Have Blue' photo is the first YF-117A SENIOR TREND prototype; 'No such person as Steve Stenson was ever commander of AFFTC'; the KGB props are surplus-store fakes. Each is falsifiable and outside the claimant's own testimony, and none has been checked and found wrong in any opened record.

edges.label: The Fouche file's DARPA invocation rests on a letter from a personnel office
edges.note: DARPA is the single most reused word in the Fouche corpus and the board's existing darpa node should carry this explicitly. The document that carries the invocation bears no classification marking, is signed by a technical sergeant in an assignments section of a personnel directorate, and is captioned by Fouche himself with the agency's name wrong, as 'Defense Advanced Research Agency'.
